Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's POC kickoff

Hi Stephanie — thanks again for the call. Quick recap from our side and a couple of follow-ups so we can scope the POC properly:

- Primary workloads: real-time transaction enrichment for debit card fraud decisions (short completions, ~40-150 tokens) and batch risk-scoring pipeline for nightly jobs (longer completions, ~1k tokens).
- Peak behavior: we expect spikes during morning/afternoon peaks; target peak concurrent in-app requests ~1,200 at 5–10 minute windows; sustained baseline concurrency ~200.
- Hard latency goals for the real-time path: p95 generation latency <= 180ms for <200-token completions. For batch we care mostly about throughput/cost.
- Streaming: we'd like streaming responses over websockets for the real-time path to start sending token deltas to our client (low client-side latency).

Two asks before next week:
1) A short note on how Redwood's connection pooling / multiplexing would handle 1,200 parallel requests — specifically around recommended pool sizing and per-connection multiplexing limits.
2) A proposed rate/quota profile for the POC (3-week sandbox) and what you'd recommend for a Dedicated reserve vs hosted tier if we need predictable SLOs.

I've attached our very rough session-density spreadsheet.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short tech call if useful.

— Alyssa
Alyssa Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudFin

Alyssa — thanks for the clear write-up and the spreadsheet (received). Below is a concise qualification and next steps so we can turn this into a concrete sandbox configuration. I'm copying Ben to validate the technical sizing.

TL;DR answers:
- Connection pooling / multiplexing: we typically recommend 1 connection per 8–12 concurrent lightweight generation streams (multiplexing via HTTP/2). For your 1,200 concurrent in-app requests, that maps to ~100–150 pooled connections if you use HTTP/2 persistent connections from your side. If you prefer a smaller pool, we can instead increase per-connection multiplexing but that raises head-of-line considerations for large streaming responses.
- POC quota profile: Hosted sandbox: 2,000 concurrent request credit, 10k tokens/sec burst window, soft QPS cap at 5k with auto-fallback. Dedicated reserved suggestion: reserve 4–8 GPUs equivalent (we'll give an estimated RU/slot chart) to hit predictable p95 latencies under your peak.
- Streaming: Websocket streaming is supported; for real-time UI we recommend framing short-chunk responses and keeping KV-cache reuse on the server-side to reduce token compute.

Action items I propose:
1) Ben to confirm concrete connection/pool numbers and a crash-rate estimate for p95 180ms.
2) Redwood to provide a formal quota proposal (sandbox hosted numbers + dedicated sizing options) by Monday.
3) Sync call Tuesday 4/21 to confirm POC start date and test plan.

Please confirm that Tuesday works or propose alternatives.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_cloudfin.docx (MAP), session_density_calc.xlsx (we reviewed).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's POC kickoff

Alyssa / Stephanie — quick technical qualification and a concrete recommended profile based on Alyssa's session-density sheet and our platform behavior. High-level assumptions: short completions ~80 tokens average for real-time path, batch jobs ~900 tokens; peak concurrent in-app = 1,200 sustained for 5–10 min.

Recommendation (sandbox hosted):
- Connection pooling: target 120 persistent HTTP/2 connections from your LB/edge into Redwood. We assume HTTP/2 with multiplexing of up to 10 concurrent streams per connection for short-completion traffic. That yields theoretical concurrency headroom ~1,200. If you use fewer connections (e.g., 60), expect slightly higher queueing and increased tail latencies; we can accept that in the sandbox but will need to monitor p95.
- Per-IP / per-key rate limits: propose starting soft cap at 5,000 RPS (requests/sec) with a per-token throttle at 12,000 tps (tokens/sec) for the sandbox; hard cap at 10,000 RPS to protect platform stability. We can tune after empirical runs.
- Reserved Dedicated suggestion: to guarantee p95 <= 180ms under peaks, reserve capacity equivalent to ~6 high-memory A100-style GPUs (we'll provide the mapping to our RU model in the formal quote). Dedicated gives you capacity isolation and ability to raise hard caps on concurrency.
- Streaming considerations: websocket connections count toward connection pool; recommend splitting streaming vs non-streaming traffic to different endpoints or routing tags to keep multiplexing predictable. For streaming with incremental tokens we recommend a per-connection multiplexing target of 4–6 streams to avoid interleaving stalls.

Observability / test plan:
- We'll instrument a small benchmark harness (we use wrk + tokenizer-aware generator) and run three 10-minute ramp tests at 50%, 100%, and 150% of your projected peak. We'll produce p50/p95/p99 token latencies and CPU/GPU occupancy traces.
- We'll add a short-lived quota bump to 2,000 concurrent credit for your sandbox account to make the initial run smooth.

Next steps I can action: produce the quantitative RU -> GPU mapping and a one-page quota table for hosted vs dedicated (by Monday). If you want, I can also propose exact LB connection counts by your ingress topology.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is really helpful and exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of quick confirmations before we lock the POC start:

1) We accept the sandbox hosted numbers you proposed (soft cap 5k RPS / 12k tps token throttle; temporary concurrent credit 2,000). Please send the formal quota attachment and any rate-limit headers we should expect so our client can handle 429s gracefully.
2) For streaming, we will route websocket traffic to a separate subdomain (stream.cloudfin.com) — please include the recommendation for 4–6 streams / connection in the quota doc.
3) Can you include a short annex that explains how Redwood's fallback to smaller model variants behaves if the platform reaches hard capacity? We need the failure/latency behavior spelled out for our risk team.

If you can get the formal quota + RU mapping + annex by EOD Monday we can target a POC start on Wednesday 4/22 with the initial benchmark slot. Also please add a HubSpot note with the sandbox credentials and the DocuSign link for the sandbox terms.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a 15-min sync if needed.

— Alyssa
